adversarial_second_pass.independent_reconstruction: A 3-year-old boy with virilization, advanced bone age, very high testosterone, prepubertal LH/FSH, undetectable hCG, normal ACTH-stimulated 17-hydroxyprogesterone, and an affected father has familial male-limited precocious puberty.
adversarial_second_pass.strongest_distractor_attack: An hCG-secreting tumor can also produce high testosterone with suppressed gonadotropins, but serum hCG is undetectable and the father-to-son recurring phenotype argues for a germline receptor disorder. CAH is closed by normal ACTH-stimulated 17-hydroxyprogesterone; central precocity requires HPG-axis activation; McCune-Albright is postzygotic and not inherited in this pattern.
adversarial_second_pass.expert_reviewer_reversal: After explicitly closing hCG-driven, adrenal, central, and mosaic GNAS pathways, the male-limited multigenerational peripheral precocity uniquely supports activating LHCGR disease.
